6. Upon a perusal of the Application in general and the investigation report submitted to the Respondent No. 1 by the District Education Officer, Mymensingh under cover of his note dated 22-7-2008 (Annexure-'G') in particular, it is evident to this Court that the District Education Officer's cover note duly conveys to the Respondent No. 1 the message of a satisfactory completion of the process of reinvestigation into the Petitioner's case apparently initiated by the Ministry itself by its Memo dated 2-4-2008 issued under Ref: শিম/শা: ১১/১২-(পুনর্বহাল) ২০০৭/৫০৩. It is further evident from the investigation report itself that for the most part allegations brought against the Petitioner have overwhelmingly been found not proven. There does appear to be an allegation with regard to financial impropriety with regard to which the finding is a fairly benign one. In this regard, the drift of Mr Haque's submissions has been of the Petitioner's expectation of a favorable conclusion to this renewed investigation process reflected in due course in an order duly and properly made and communicated and by reason of which the rigors of the operation in particular of the Impugned Order of 6-11-2007 (Annexure- 'F') ought, accordingly, to be wholly removed. 

 7. Upon a consideration of the above, this Court finds that the procrastination evident in the prolonged inaction of the Respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 in particular in finally deciding upon the investigation report of 2008 has resultantly led the Petitioner to be unduly prejudiced by the sustained operation of the Impugned Orders over a long' period. Such inaction and silence are, in the circumstances; found both unreasonable and arbitrary. It is incumbent upon these Respondents to bear in mind that the real issue here, as so succinctly observed by Sedley, J in R vs Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food ex p Humble reported in [1995] 2 All ER 714, is one of ensuring and maintaining fairness in public administration. By that reason, this Court finds that it has thus far been unfair on the part of the Respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 to frustrate the Petitioner's legitimate expectation that as decision-makers they would have in due course arrived at a firm decision long ago and not sat on the material already before them for as long as they have. This Court is disinclined to condone such protracted inactivity. The least that is now required of these Respondents is that they not only act promptly but with fairness and are indeed seen to be acting with fairness in a manner geared to: promote public confidence in the administration process (MP. Industries Ltd. vs. India reported in AIR 1966 SC 671; Ram Chander vs. India reported in AIR 1986 SC 1175). To that end, this Court finds it to be incumbent on the Respondents to additionally favour the Petitioner with a reasoned decision or order. In this regard, this Court subscribes to Lord Denning's observation that "the giving of reasons is one of the fundamentals of good administration." (Breen vs Amalgamated Engineering Union reported in 1971) 1 All ER 1148). This Court is fully satisfied that fairness alone demands such reasoned decision to be given regardless of whether the said Respondents are otherwise obliged or not under the law to provide reasons for their decision.
